description: One real estate parcel: where it is, how big it is, who holds title, what it was last appraised at, and — when it is on the balance sheet — which Fixed Asset carries it. The unit is the parcel as the county assessor knows it, because that is the unit an appraisal, a tax bill and a deed all agree on.

fields.description: What this parcel is called in conversation: 'Red Camp', 'Mill Creek', 'Packing House'. The docname is built from this and the owning entity's abbreviation, so two entities may each have a 'Home Place'.
fields.label: Parcel Name

fields.description: A short key for this parcel — 'MC' for Mill Creek, 'RC' for Red Camp. Left blank it is derived from the parcel name, and the derivation is what every Field, Irrigation Zone and Housing Unit docname on this parcel is suffixed with. Change it and those docnames do not follow: it is a key, not a label.
fields.label: Abbreviation

fields.description: The company whose books track this parcel. Where title is held by an entity that is not a company on this site — a trust, a sibling LLC — record that in Title Holder and leave this as the company doing the tracking.
fields.label: Owning Entity

fields.description: The county assessor's parcel number, exactly as printed on the tax statement. This is the only identifier a third party will recognise.
fields.label: Assessor Parcel ID
Use Type
fields.options:
Orchard
Farmstead

Residential

Bare Land
Mixed
Other

fields.description: Two-letter state or province code. A county with no state is not an address.
fields.label: State

fields.description: Deeded or GIS acreage. Say which in Notes when the two disagree, because they usually do.
fields.label: Acreage

fields.description: Who actually holds title, when that is not the owning entity itself. Points at the Related Party register so the legal name lives in one place.
fields.label: Title Holder

fields.description: Fee simple market value from the most recent appraisal. Not a book value: what the asset cost is on the Fixed Asset record, and the two are meant to differ.
fields.label: Appraised Value

fields.description: The effective date of the appraisal, which is not the date the report was delivered.
fields.label: Appraised As Of

fields.description: Who signed the appraisal, and their designation.
fields.label: Appraiser

fields.description: The archived appraisal report. A value with no document behind it is a number somebody remembered.
fields.label: Appraisal Document

fields.description: The Fixed Asset that carries this parcel on the balance sheet, when there is one. Land is not depreciated; improvements on it usually are, and those are separate Assets.
fields.label: Related Asset

fields.description: Every conveyance that brought this parcel onto this entity's books. Empty for a parcel that was registered here and has never moved, which is most of them.
fields.label: Conveyance History

fields.description: Written by convey_parcel and read-only in practice. A conveyance deletes the record on the old entity's books and creates this one, so the surviving record is the only place the history can live — the row names the entity it came from and the docname it had there.
fields.label: Conveyance Events

fields.description: The shape on the ground, and on a parcel it is the OUTER one: every Field, Irrigation Zone and Housing Unit registered here is expected to sit inside it. Everything below the polygon is DERIVED from it on save and must not be edited by hand — a figure a person can change independently of the polygon is a figure that will disagree with it, and the disagreement surfaces as a geofence saying no to somebody standing in the right place.
fields.label: Boundary

fields.description: The parcel boundary as a GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon, in [longitude, latitude] degrees. Set it with set_parcel_boundary rather than by hand: the tool validates the shape and recomputes everything derived from it. A parcel traced off the assessor's map is the usual source, and it is the shape the deed and the tax bill both describe.
fields.label: Boundary (GeoJSON)

fields.description: Computed. Where a map opens, and the cheap first cut for a distance query. For a shape whose true centroid falls outside it — a parcel wrapped round somebody else's inholding — this is an interior point instead, because centring on the inholding is centring on ground that is not this parcel's.
fields.label: Centroid Latitude

fields.description: Computed. See Centroid Latitude.
fields.label: Centroid Longitude

fields.description: Computed. A bounding box is a guaranteed superset of the shape it bounds, which is what makes it the only safe cheap prefilter for 'is this point inside' — a candidate set built from it can never miss the right answer.
fields.label: Bounding Box (GeoJSON)

fields.description: Computed. JSON of {resolution: [cells]} at resolutions 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, holding every cell the shape TOUCHES. Not every cell whose centre is inside it: a centre-based fill returns nothing for a shape smaller than one cell, and an index built on it would answer 'on no parcel' for a point plainly on one.
fields.label: H3 Cells

fields.description: Computed from the polygon by spherical excess. This is a different number from the deeded or GIS acreage above and both are worth having: a deed, an assessor's map and a GIS trace routinely disagree by a few percent. A gap over 5% is reported; over 25% the boundary is refused, because at that point one of the two figures is about a different piece of ground.
fields.label: Computed Area (acres)
